title: Senior Rollout Manager (f/m/x) – DACH
description:
Your mission IONITY baut ein europaweites Netzwerk von High-Power-Ladestationen auf und betreibt dieses. Als Senior Rollout Manager übernimmst du die Verantwortung für die erfolgreiche Umsetzung mehrerer Ladestandorte in der DACH-Region – von der Rollout-Planung und der Standortvorbereitung über die Bauphase, Inbetriebnahme und Abnahme bis zur Übergabe an Operations. Du überführst komplexe, funktionsübergreifende Projekte in einen planbaren und verlässlichen Rollout neuer Standorte.
Die Rolle verbindet Projektmanagement, Infrastrukturentwicklung und Stakeholder-Management. Du koordinierst interne Teams, Behörden, Grundstückseigentümer, Netzbetreiber, Baufirmen, Installationspartner und spezialisierte Partner auf gemeinsame Meilensteine, Entscheidungen und Qualitätsstandards. Deine Arbeit leistet einen direkten Beitrag zum Wachstum des europäischen IONITY Netzwerks, sowie einem zuverlässigen Ladeerlebnis für Elektrofahrzeugfahrerinnen und -fahrer aus ganz Europa. Jede neue Ladesäule als Ergebnis deiner Arbeit beschleunigt die Verkehrswende und ist ein wichtiger Beitrag für eine emissionsfreie Mobilität.
- Du übernimmst die ganzheitliche Verantwortung für die Umsetzung eines Portfolios von HPC-Ladestandorten in der DACH-Region, mit besonderem Fokus auf die komplexesten, risikoreichsten oder strategisch wichtigsten Standorte. Über den gesamten Projektlebenszyklus hinweg steuerst du Umfang, Zeitplan, Abhängigkeiten, Risikoexponierung, Kostenrisiken, Qualität, Sicherheit, Compliance und die betriebliche Umsetzungsreife.
- Du übersetzt die Rollout-Ziele in integrierte Standort- und Portfolioumsetzungspläne, definierst Prioritäten, Reihenfolgen, Meilensteine und Abhängigkeiten und stellst eine klare Governance sicher – von der Standortentwicklung und Genehmigungsplanung über die Bauphase und Inbetriebnahme bis zur Übergabe an den Betrieb.
- Du führst die funktionsübergreifende Umsetzung über die Bereiche Planung und Genehmigung, Bau, Netzanschluss, Logistik etc. hinweg, treibst zeitnahe Entscheidungen voran, löst Konflikte und stellst sicher, dass kritische Schnittstellen zwischen Grundstück, Tiefbau, Elektrotechnik, Netzanschluss, Installation der Ladehardware, Prüfung und Inbetriebnahme aktiv gesteuert werden.
- Du steuerst externe Planungsbüros, Auftragnehmer, Installationsunternehmen und weitere Umsetzungspartner direkt, setzt klare Erwartungen, überwachst die Leistung, steuerst die operative Umsetzung sowie kommerzielle Risiken und stellst sicher, dass die Partner die vereinbarten Ergebnisse liefern.
- Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für das Risiko-, Änderungs- und Maßnahmenmanagement des Portfolios, identifizierst kritische Risiken frühzeitig, definierst Gegenmaßnahmen und führst Wiederherstellungspläne für verspätete, blockierte oder erheblich vom Plan abweichende Standorte. Dabei schützt du Umsetzungsqualität, Sicherheit und Compliance.
- Du triffst Entscheidungen innerhalb deines übertragenen Verantwortungs- und Entscheidungsrahmens und erstellst klare Entscheidungsvorlagen für den Country Manager DACH, sofern eine Eskalation erforderlich ist. Du stellst tragfähige Optionen, Auswirkungen und Empfehlungen dar und wägst dabei Zeitplan, Kosten, Qualität, technische Machbarkeit und die Anforderungen der Stakeholder gegeneinander ab.
- Du baust vertrauensvolle Beziehungen zu Behörden, Netzbetreibern, Grundstückseigentümern, lokalen Stakeholdern und Umsetzungspartnern auf und pflegst diese, vertrittst IONITY auch in komplexen Gesprächen professionell und löst Genehmigungs-, Netzanschluss-, Grundstücks-, Bau- und sonstige Umsetzungshindernisse pragmatisch.
- Du erstellst prägnante und entscheidungsorientierte Berichte für Senior Stakeholder, einschließlich Fortschritt, prognostizierter Termine, Prognosesicherheit, wesentlicher Risiken, Kosten- und kommerzieller Risiken, Partnerleistung, Maßnahmen zur Planwiederherstellung sowie der erforderlichen Entscheidungen, um das Portfolio auf Kurs zu halten.
- Du etablierst und verbesserst kontinuierlich Rollout-Standards, Governance-Routinen, Vorlagen und Umsetzungsleitfäden. Auf Basis gewonnener Erkenntnisse erhöhst du die Planbarkeit, Qualität, Skalierbarkeit und Umsetzungseffektivität des Rollouts im gesamten DACH-Netzwerk.

Your profile - Du bist ein Teamplayer und arbeitest auch unter Zeitdruck mit einem hohen Anspruch an Qualität.
- Du verfügst über nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Leitung der Umsetzung komplexer Infrastruktur-, Bau-, Energie-, Mobilitäts-, Telekommunikations- oder vergleichbarer Rollout-Programme über mehrere Standorte hinweg, ideralerweise im Bereich HPC Ladeinfrastruktur.
- Du kannst eine Erfolgsbilanz bei der Übernahme von Ergebnisverantwortung über den gesamten Umsetzungslebenszyklus vorweisen – und nicht nur für einzelne Projektaufgaben oder Arbeitspakete.
- Du verfügst über ausgeprägte Kenntnisse in Programm- und Projektsteuerung, einschließlich integrierter Planung, Risikomanagement, Abhängigkeitsmanagement, Änderungssteuerung und Reporting auf Senior-Ebene.
- Du hast Erfahrung in der Steuerung externer Partner sowie in der Einflussnahme auf interne Stakeholder in einer Matrixorganisation. Du trittst sicher auf, stellst bestehende Ansätze konstruktiv infrage, triffst Entscheidungen und eskalierst Themen, wenn dies erforderlich ist.
- Du verfügst über ein fundiertes praktisches Verständnis der Schnittstellen zwischen Standortentwicklung, Genehmigungsplanung, Tiefbau, Elektrotechnik, Netzanschluss, Inbetriebnahme und Übergabe an den Betrieb.
- Du kommunizierst klar und strukturiert auf Deutsch und Englisch.
- Du besitzt einen gültigen Führerschein und bist bereit, regelmäßig mit Teams an den Standorten zusammenzuarbeiten.
- Du hast Erfahrung in der Umsetzung von Ladeinfrastruktur für Elektrofahrzeuge, Anlagen im Bereich erneuerbare Energien oder anderer dezentraler, kundenorientierter Infrastruktur.
- Du verfügst über etablierte Arbeitsbeziehungen zu Behörden, Netzbetreibern, Grundstückseigentümern und Baupartnern in einem oder mehreren DACH-Märkten.
- Du hast Erfahrung mit Schnittstellen zu Hochspannungs- oder elektrotechnischer Infrastruktur sowie mit der Inbetriebnahme und Übergabe in ein operatives Netzwerk.
- Du verfügst über gute Anwenderkenntnisse in AutoCAD und Microsoft Office, einschließlich fortgeschrittener Excel-Kenntnisse oder vergleichbarer Projektsteuerungs-Tools.
- Du hast ein einschlägiges Hochschulstudium, eine technische Qualifikation oder vergleichbare berufliche Erfahrung in den Bereichen Ingenieurwesen, Bauwesen, Infrastruktur oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet.

description:
Your mission IONITY is building the backbone of electric mobility in Europe. Founded by leading automotive manufacturers, we operate Europe’s largest high-power charging network across 24 countries, enabling seamless long-distance travel for EV drivers. With thousands of charging points already in operation and significant expansion ahead, IONITY is evolving beyond charging infrastructure into a broader mobility, energy and digital platform. 

As Senior People Ops & Payroll Manager , you'll ensure IONITY's People Operations and payroll run accurately, on time and with care across our multi-country European setup. This is a hands-on role for someone who knows payroll inside out, enjoys making processes cleaner and more scalable, and wants the admin side of work to feel effortless for employees. 

You'll own the payroll cycle end to end, keep our employee data and lifecycle processes in great shape, and be the go-to partner for our external payroll providers, People Partners and employees. 

What you'll do 
- Own the monthly payroll process across countries, including preparatory payroll accounting, inputs, handovers and sign-off with external payroll providers. 
- Keep employee master data in Personio & Deel accurate, compliant and audit-ready . 
- Manage core lifecycle processes (onboarding, leave, offboarding), including work time accounts, eAU administration and work certificates. 
- Act as a main contact for payroll providers, tax advisors and auditors, and resolve issues quickly and professionally. 
- Spot friction in processes, systems and workflows, then fix it, using automation and exploring AI where they add real value. 
- Support the alignment of employee benefits across countries while respecting local requirements. 
- Partner closely with People Partners and Finance so payroll, reporting and People processes join up. 
- Answer employee questions on pay and HR admin with clarity and discretion. 
- Guide or mentor junior team members, own larger process and system projects, and act as a sparring partner to People leadership. 

Your profile - 5 years of experience in payroll and People / HR Operations, ideally including German payroll. 
- Experience coordinating payroll across multiple countries, working with external providers. 
- Strong knowledge of relevant labor law, tax and social security requirements, with a willingness to learn new countries. 
- Hands-on experience with Deel & Personio is a strong plus. 
- A structured, reliable and discreet way of working, with a real eye for detail and deadlines. 
- A pragmatic, improvement-minded approach: you like clean processes, but not bureaucracy for its own sake. 
- Curiosity about how systems, automation and AI can make work better. 
- Fluent English and German; another European language is a bonus. 
- Proven ownership of multi-country payroll and experience leading process or system improvements, or guiding others.

title: Senior Software Engineer – IT Risk & Pricing (m/f/d)
description:
Your new team: As a Senior Software Engineer (m/f/d) at auxmoney, you’ll join our IT Risk & Pricing team, where we build backend systems and services that support risk decisioning, pricing, and data-driven product logic. The work is backend-heavy, involving complex technical problem-solving and close integration with data/analytics workflows. 

In this role, you’ll design and deliver impactful features, help evolve a scalable, resilient architecture, and take end-to-end ownership from concept through production. You’ll work closely with analysts/data scientists, product managers, and business stakeholders to ship high-quality solutions and continuously improve our engineering standards. If you are passionate about writing clean, maintainable code, solving complex technical challenges, and building software that delivers real value, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

What you can expect: - Architecture & System Design: Identify and address architectural limitations, make pragmatic trade-offs, and help evolve systems toward scalability, reliability, and long-term maintainability.
- Technical Leadership: Act as a trusted technical expert by promoting engineering best practices, facilitating technical discussions, and helping teams align on high-quality solutions.

- Execution & Delivery: Break down complex initiatives into manageable workstreams and deliver incremental value through iterative development.
- Impact & Knowledge Sharing: Champion engineering excellence, share knowledge proactively, and support the professional growth of colleagues.
- Collaboration & Problem Solving: Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders, actively contribute to design reviews, and address root causes of recurring technical challenges.
- Ownership & Mentorship: Take responsibility for challenging projects and guide team members through technical mentoring and hands-on support.

description:
Role Hive Robotics is building Europe’s first full-stack orchestration platform for unmanned systems: connecting, controlling, and commanding multi-vendor drone and robot swarms. Our RF communication systems are Made in Germany, deployed on active frontlines, and targeting a highly valued tactical communication market with zero sovereign alternatives today.
As our first dedicated Account Executive, you own the sales pipeline: every opportunity from a lead to a signed contract. You take over our existing customer accounts and drive the opportunities our founders and Business Development have opened, with the first new deals expected to close within 3 months. You currently report to the CEO.
This role is customer-facing by design: expect 30–50% travel to customer sites, procurement offices, partners and trade fairs across Germany and Europe, sometimes internationally. The rest of the time you work alongside Engineering, Product Management and our Field Application Engineers.

Responsibilities - Own the funnel from the first qualified conversation to signature. Our founders and Business Development open doors with customers, partners and the wider ecosystem. From there the opportunity is yours: you qualify it, drive it and close it, pulling the founders back in only when a deal needs them. Leads you generate yourself count just as much, this isn't exclusively BD's territory.
- Qualify hard and early. Run discovery against a fixed gate (pain, budget, decision-making unit, timing) before we invest engineering time in a technical deep dive, and keep a clear next step with a date on every opportunity.
- Lead the customer's buying team through a hardware buying cycle: end users, engineers, procurement, legal and IT, across long evaluations, equipment trials run as projects, integration questions and security reviews.
- Orchestrate the deal team. Bring in our engineers and Field Application Engineers for demos, trials and technical deep dives, and Product Management for configuration and fit. You decide when a deal needs them and what they're there to do.
- Own our active customers commercially: account plans, follow-on orders, upsells and expansion into new units and use cases, every escalation that touches the relationship, and regular account reviews with the Field Application Engineer who owns adoption.
- Turn deployed systems into the next deal: reference visits, customer quotes and case material that you or the founders can use to open new accounts.
- Own the offer: configuration and pricing, terms and conditions, the cost-benefit case on the customer's own data, and the project plan to signature. Lead our responses to RFPs and tenders where they apply, and build the templates so every proposal starts from a proven base.
- Get a trial agreement signed before any trial starts: scope, duration, success criteria, pilot price and the path to the main contract. You drive it, Operations owns the paperwork.
- Close, and hand over cleanly. Request the contract from Operations, keep the customer and the internal side moving, and sign. Then hand over to Operations as a confirmed customer order and to the Field Application Engineer for onboarding.

- Hands-on daily work in a CRM and a disciplined qualification method (e.g. MEDDPICC): your forecast is something the company can plan on

Nice to Have - An existing network or experience selling to the DACH defense ecosystem: armed forces, procurement offices, primes, integrators

- Experience building a sales pipeline or sales function from scratch rather than inheriting one

description:
Atolls is the world's largest community-driven shopping platform, active in 20+ markets. 

We help millions make smarter spending decisions across discovery, evaluation, and (re-)purchase by connecting people with the right brands and retailers.

Our 1,000+ team across 10 countries builds products used every day at global scale, where you'll have real ownership and see your impact. Want to shape the destinations people rely on to shop with confidence? Keep reading.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Java/SpringBoot) to join our Shopping team in Berlin . As a key part of our team, you'll be directly involved in building and enhancing the digital destinations our users rely on throughout their shopping journeys.

Your contributions will help shape how millions of consumers interact with our platforms, guiding them to make smart, fair, and rewarding choices.

- A culture that values personal and professional development, with internal mobility opportunities.

- A supportive and open-minded team that embraces diverse perspectives and innovative ideas.

- 32 days of paid vacation plus your birthday off, giving you the time you need to recharge.

- A flexible hybrid working scheme to balance work and life.

- Access to a learning budget and internal training to help you grow in your role.

- Mental health coaching to support your well-being.

- Regular global and local get-togethers to celebrate successes and build connections.

- The possibility of taking a sabbatical after three years with the company.

- A cloud-based company setup, providing flexibility and collaboration opportunities no matter where you are.

*These are global benefits that apply to all employees, with additional local perks based on your location. 

Responsibilities: 

In this role, you will:

- Design and develop modern architectures using Java, AWS technologies, microservices, NoSQL & RDBMS, event-driven architectures, etc.

- Be involved in the inception, development, and delivery of various features and products on an ambitious and challenging product roadmap.

- Take responsibility for our solution architecture and contribute to improving it in terms of performance, security, scalability, modularity, and operational efficiency.

- Be involved in multiple projects at the same time and manage your time effectively.

- Conduct knowledge-sharing sessions through presentations and hands-on tasks that help practice new technologies.

Your Profile: 

We're looking for someone with 6+ years of experience, who is dedicated to creating exceptional user experiences and driving innovation.

- 6+ years of experience in designing and developing complex modular applications from technical planning to implementation within a client-side framework as well as server-side.

- Strong knowledge and active hands-on experience of Java and SpringBoot .

- Object-oriented programming concepts with application to concurrent event-based systems.

- Previous knowledge and experience with JS (TypeScript, NodeJS), HTML, CSS and React/Angular.

- Knowledge of AWS technologies such as DynamoDB, Elasticsearch, relational and NoSQL databases, EventBridge and messaging and queuing solutions like SQS, SNS (or any other cloud platform like Google Cloud or Azure).

- Experience with GraphQL, federation and Supergraph concepts.

- Excellent understanding of common design/architectural patterns, and the ability to produce elegant designs in modular/microservice design patterns.

- Logical, analytic thinking, structured and target-oriented approach, very good problem-solving skills.

- Passion for delivering clean code, unit/integration tests and maintainable documentation.

- Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies and DevOps best practices.

- Demonstrated ability to support and mentor more junior members of a software development team.

- BS degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Excellent communication skills and fluency in written and spoken English.

Our hiring process :

- TA Call : Meet one of our Talent Experts and get to know Atolls better.

- Technical Round : Focus on the technical aspects of the role (Through a Live Case) , and meet your potential manager.

- Final Round : Meet other Atollians 🏝️
It varies from 1 to 3 interviews

Be part of a destination where your work helps millions of people make better decisions every day. One focused application is all we need. If you truly fit more than one role, you're welcome to apply to up to three. This helps us match you with the right opportunity faster.

We review every application with equal care and will reach out if your profile aligns. Apply now with your CV in English.

- Solid on GCP or an equivalent cloud: containers, networking and IAM basics, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting. You have owned infrastructure, not just deployed onto it
- Comfortable with high-volume time-series data: ingestion, data quality, backfills, and the everyday reality of late, missing and duplicated readings
- You have seen a few things. Enough production years behind you to know which trade-offs come back to bite, when the boring option is the right one, and how to make a call with incomplete information instead of waiting for certainty
- Kubernetes knowledge at the level of running it, not only deploying to it.

- You run what you build: monitoring, alerting, and the occasional early morning debugging a pipeline

This is a hands-on technical role for someone who wants to own how analytics get built. You will take approved metric definitions and business questions and turn them into the models and metric logic in Snowflake and dbt, the dashboards, and the semantic layer and data products people use every day. 

You will own the analytics engineering for key areas of the business: understanding what needs to be measured, building the models, validating the logic, delivering the reporting, and keeping it accurate and reliable over time. - Build a small set of high-value dashboards in Tableau (and Sigma, as we evolve the stack). 

- Contribute to the semantic layer so certified metrics are reusable across BI tools, Snowflake Cortex, and embedded analytics. 

- Automate recurring analytics work, with the tests and monitoring that keep it trustworthy. 

- Partner with analysts and stakeholders to interpret data, build context, and surface risks before they are asked. 

- Contribute to brand-facing data products used by account teams and manufacturer partners. 

What you'll bring 

- 5+ years in analytics engineering, data analytics, or a similar technical analytics role, owning data models and reporting that a business relies on. 

- Expert SQL on large and complex datasets. You write clean, efficient queries and can debug someone else's logic as easily as your own. 

- Strong hands-on Snowflake and dbt (or a comparable modern data stack), including dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing, and documentation. 

- Strong Tableau skills. Sigma, Looker, or similar a plus. 

- Strong judgment on metric design: grain, denominators, filters, time zones, deduplication, and the ways a correct number can still mislead. 

- Commercial sense and curiosity. You want to understand why a number matters, can explain what a change means for the business, and hold a position under questioning. 

- An automation mindset. When you see something repetitive or fragile, your instinct is to find a better way to build it. 

- Comfort working across several domains at once, prioritizing your own work, and managing stakeholders directly. 

- Clear, concise communication and the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences. 

Preferred

In your first 30 days you understand the stack, the models, the people, and the priorities in your domains, and you have your first dbt change merged. 

By 60 days you are producing real work independently: agreed metric definitions implemented, your first certified models and dashboards in use, and a plan for the first manual workflow you will automate. 

By 90 days stakeholders treat you as their analytics partner rather than a request queue. Your models are trusted, your dashboards are used without hand-holding, and your automation is reducing real manual effort.

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

The Team 

BizOps is the team that keeps its finger on the pulse of business performance: continuously, rigorously, and across multiple dimensions at once. We turn raw operational and financial data into actionable intelligence, surfacing what is happening, why it is happening, and what to expect next , for the operators, executives, and functional teams who run the business day to day.

We are not a reporting function that produces outputs on request. We work continuously, proactively watching, delivering, and questioning whether the signal is real, acting as "first responders" to surprising deviations from expectation and using what we learn to drive faster, better decision-making for the business at large.

Our work spans the full stack of analytics: from the warehouse models that make metrics trustworthy, to the monitoring systems that catch problems early, to the reports and dashboards that make performance visible, to the deep-dive investigations that explain what the numbers mean and what we should do about it.

We anchor our analysis to the right reference points: how performance compares to plan, to prior periods, and to what we'd expect, and we bring causal rigour when the business needs to know whether an action actually worked.

The culture within the team is informal, fast-paced and entrepreneurial. Given the growth of the business and the level of senior stakeholder exposure, progression in the team can be fast.

The Role 

Deliveroo is hiring a Senior Data Scientist to join BizOps, based in our London HQ (hybrid, minimum three days per week in the office).

This role is largely project-based: starting from a strategic or performance question, you'll combine data, business context, and structured problem-solving to provide the insights that drive decision-making at a global level with senior stakeholders. You will own delivery end-to-end, from the messy, ambiguous question to a rigorous, trustworthy, and actionable answer.

You'll be equally comfortable building the systems that make performance visible and going deep on the investigations that explain it. One week you might diagnose why a key market has moved away from plan; the next, identify the drivers behind a change in customer or operational performance; the next, build monitoring that helps teams spot and understand emerging issues earlier.

Success in this role requires building effective working relationships across Deliveroo, particularly with international markets, as well as the Data Science, Operations, Commercial, and Finance teams.

What You'll Be Doing 

- 
Answer the questions that matter, continuously. Maintain a rigorous view on business performance: Are we on track against our goals? What's changed? How does this compare with what we expected? What should we expect next? Then go further: Why is it happening, what matters most, and what should we do about it?" 

- 
Own delivery end-to-end. Independently identify, define, and deliver impactful work aligned with business goals, operating with minimal guidance to ship fast, high-quality solutions.

- 
Navigate ambiguity. Deconstruct broad, ambiguous problem spaces into structured analytical roadmaps, and understand how your work intersects with adjacent systems and teams.

- 
Build for scale, not one-offs. Build the pipelines, models, dashboards, monitoring, and investigative tooling that make performance visible and reliable. Automate wherever possible; redoing analyses by hand is slow and error-prone.

- 
Measure impact with discipline. Design measurement strategies from simple A/B tests to quasi-experimental designs (synthetic control, difference-in-differences, event studies) when trials aren't feasible, always with conservative, assumption-explicit language.

- 
Be a first responder. Surface deviations before they become escalations, and be just as willing to give the confident "this is noise, no action needed" as the alarm.

- 
Communicate to influence. Translate complex findings into clear, simple, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences that shape roadmaps and decisions.

- 
Raise the bar. Contribute to the broader Analytics community, improve shared approaches and best practices, and help build data literacy across the business.

What You'll Need to Thrive

- 
Experience in an analytical or data science role, such as data analytics, data science, forecasting, planning, strategy analytics, or a similar discipline. Experience in logistics, e-commerce, marketplaces, or another fast-moving, customer-focused business is useful but not essential.

- 
Proficiency with SQL and a scripting language such as Python or R, alongside experience with BI or visualisation tooling such as Looker, Tableau, or similar.

- 
Comfortable using modern AI-assisted tools to work efficiently while maintaining high standards of accuracy and reproducibility.

- 
A pragmatic approach to problem-solving: you can balance analytical rigour with speed, adapt your approach to the importance of the decision, and focus effort where it will have the greatest impact.

- 
Effective problem-solving: you can take an ambiguous question, identify the underlying problem or decision, develop hypotheses, and use data and business context to reach a clear point of view.

- 
Experience with experimentation and/or causal inference is a strong plus: the ability to unpick insights and steer strategic decisions.

- 
Excellent communication skills, in person, in writing, and in code, with the ability to translate business needs into analytical problems and complex findings into simple recommendations.

-

You'll spend the majority of your time as a proactive, high-energy complaint handler: resolving complex disputes and keeping pace with our regulatory deadlines. This is much more than a standard complaint handler role: alongside resolving complex disputes, you'll lead our monthly complaints reviews, drive root cause analysis, and step up complaints handling processes for the region.

Who you are: 

- You're a natural complaint handler – you take ownership of a steady caseload, resolve issues objectively and fairly, and can turn a messy, technical problem into a clear explanation for the customer. You also have extensive knowledge of UK regulations including DISP and the FOS complaints handling process.

- You're organised and deadline-driven – you manage your own schedule to make sure every case is resolved within the required legal timeframes, without needing to be chased

- You're detailed-orientated – you can prepare thorough case files, gather evidence, and represent Airwallex professionally in front of the Financial Ombudsman Service

- You're ready to step up – you’ll run our monthly complaints meetings and drive root cause analysis across EMEA.

- You're a great collaborator – you'll work closely with internal teams to fix the root cause of issues.

- You’re ambitious – you're excited by the idea of shaping how we run complaints across EMEA as our first hire in the function, and by helping us build how we use AI to handle complaints at scale

Responsibilities 

- Manage your caseload: Take ownership of a steady stream of complaints, meeting daily targets while maintaining high standards.

- Meet regulatory timelines: Manage your own schedule to ensure every case is resolved within the required legal timeframes

- Lead on regulator escalations: Manage cases that reach the Financial Ombudsman Service, preparing thorough case files, gathering evidence, and drafting Airwallex's final position

- Own the regulator relationship: Act as the day-to-day point of contact with the Ombudsman, keeping our responses professional, timely and factual

- Lead our EMEA complaints reviews: Run our monthly complaints meetings, bringing visibility to trends, volumes and priorities across the region

- Drive root cause analysis: Work cross-functionally with internal teams to identify why issues occur, and lead the push for long-term fixes rather than one-off resolutions

- Help build our complaints AI capability: As volumes grow, help shape how we use AI to handle complaints more efficiently at scale

What you'll bring: 

- 5+ years' experience handling regulated complaints, ideally within financial services

- Strong working knowledge of DISP and other relevant complaints-handling regulation

- Experience preparing cases for, and liaising with, regulators such as the Financial Ombudsman Service

- A track record of meeting productivity and quality targets in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment

- Strong verbal and written communication skills in English

- Experience driving root cause analysis or process improvement cross-functionally

title: Labour AI Specialist
description:
About Sona 

Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment.

We think that's because the problem needed AI, not just better software, before it was solvable. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. Used properly, that data lets agents take on real parts of running the business rather than just reporting on it. That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here .

About the Role 

Sona's Labour AI team builds the forecasting, rules and scheduling tools that help hospitality and retail businesses get staffing right. Getting the tooling built is one problem. Getting it to actually work for a specific site, with its own trading patterns, staff and quirks, is another. That's what this role owns; working directly with customers to turn Sona's forecasting and scheduling tools into labour models that actually get used on site.

You'll derive labour rules from real trading data, spend time on site with customer teams to learn how the business actually runs, and build the trust with site managers that makes a new workload model stick. You'll present the impact and ROI of that work to customer executives and general managers, and act as the subject matter expert for labour optimisation in sales conversations.

You'll also be the person site managers trust enough to change how they staff, and the person customer executives and General Managers trust enough to back the changes you're proposing. That's an influence job as much as an analytical one. You'll report back to customer leadership on the impact, in numbers they can take to their own board.

There's no fixed playbook here. You'll adapt the same underlying labour model across different business types, from QSR to premium dining to retail.

Responsibilities 

- Derive labour rules from real trading data using Sona's tooling and your own operational knowledge

- Spend time on site with customer teams, learning practical realities like stock deliveries and close-down procedures

- Build trust with site managers so workload models actually get followed

- Present impact and ROI to customer executives and general managers, winning buy-in for operational change

- Act as the labour optimisation subject matter expert in sales conversations

- Work across the full portfolio of live customer projects, picking up work as priorities shift between accounts

Requirements 

- An operational background in hospitality, retail, or a similar hourly-workforce, fluctuating-demand business. You understand how the business runs day to day, not just how to analyse it from the outside

- Confident presenting to and winning buy-in from customer executives, general managers and boards, and comfortable holding your own with competing agendas in the room

- Comfortable with technology and confident picking up new tools quickly, including using AI tools in your own workflow

- Able to look into the data yourself and make decisions from what you find

- Comfortable operating without a fixed playbook

- Excited about using AI in your day-to-day work to 10x your output

- Bonus: a retail or workforce-management background where the underlying concepts transfer to hospitality

- Bonus: a commercial finance background with genuine credibility in front of operators

Benefits 

- Salary: £85,000 - £100,000

- Hybrid working, 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho), with customer-facing travel

title: Senior Product Manager (JetBrains Context)
description:
Coding agents are only as good as the context they're given. Most explore a repository like a new hire on day one – grepping, opening files, guessing. JetBrains Context replaces that with actual knowledge of your whole codebase and resources, served to any agent that asks. If you want to own the layer that decides what an agent knows before it writes a single line, this is for you.

About JetBrains 

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do 

As agents get better at searching for themselves, what is the durable value of a managed retrieval layer? We need someone with an opinionated answer to own JetBrains Context as a product – defining what it is for, who it is for, how we measure success, and where it goes next.

This is a hands-on role where you'll manage the product from a terminal and agent session rather than slides. You'll bridge the technical core and cross-functional teams: collaborating closely with engineering and ML teams on indexing pipelines and retrieval quality, working with Air, IDE, and Junie teams on integrations, and partnering with marketing, developer advocacy, sales, and customer success on positioning and adoption. You'll take full ownership of defining problem statements, setting explicit trade-offs, and balancing cost, latency, and freshness across the platform.

Day to day, you will:

- Build and maintain a deep working understanding of chunking, embeddings, index freshness, retrieval, reranking, and agent-facing surfaces.

- Define and defend an opinionated vision for the product's evolution, including explicit target audiences, use cases, and key success metrics.

- Translate product strategy into actionable problem statements, priorities, plans, and milestones with an explicit definition of “done”.

- Communicate product direction clearly to engineering, leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, customers, and prospects.

- Analyze competing context and code-search products through direct use to establish clear differentiators and identify gaps.

- Define core operational and product metrics – index freshness, retrieval quality, agent task outcomes, adoption, retention, and unit economics – to guide decision-making.

- Represent the product externally by sharing roadmaps, publishing updates, speaking to developer audiences, and gathering community feedback.

- Partner with ML teams on model evaluation and platform teams on service scale, reliability, and cost.

What you’ll bring 

- A well-argued point of view on where AI-first development is going and what agents genuinely need from a context layer.

- Comfort with technical depth across embeddings, retrieval quality, sub-agents, tool-calling, indexing costs, and API design.

- The habit of using the product you build daily alongside competitors' tools.

- Communication that adapts to different audiences, from staff engineers and enterprise architects to conference attendees.

- A data-informed approach that combines telemetry, evaluation results, customer conversations, and market signals.

- Comfort with ambiguity and a preference for defining a new category over copying an existing one.

What you’ll need 

- Proven experience owning a complex developer, platform, or infrastructure product end to end, including strategy and roadmap.

- Hands-on familiarity with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows.

- The technical capability to work directly with engineering on retrieval behavior, APIs, data models, and integration surfaces.

- The ability to define metrics for quality-sensitive products and build evaluation habits that maintain product standards.

- Experience communicating a product externally through written content, talks, or community engagement.

- Practical experience with search, retrieval, RAG, developer search, or static analysis at scale is a plus.

What success looks like 

Within your first months, you'll form and share a clear thesis for what JetBrains Context is and is not – one the engineering team recognizes as theirs and leadership can invest in. You'll establish a metrics story that distinguishes real retrieval quality from vanity usage, a roadmap with clear trade-offs, and a documented evaluation of serious competitors.

Longer term, success means JetBrains Context becomes a deliberate choice for developers and organizations, agents get measurably better answers because it exists, enterprises adopt it for its governance and scale, and the market clearly understands its unique value because you've communicated it effectively.

Why join JetBrains? 

- Strong base salary. We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience.

- Flexible work location. Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office.

- Remote work. Spend up to 30 days per year working remotely from abroad.

- Extra time off. More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love.

- Medical insurance allowance. Enjoy peace of mind for you and your family

- Learning and development opportunities. Access to conferences, courses, and language classes.

- Language classes. Pick up the local language or sharpen your English skills.

- Fuel your day. Enjoy a hot meal or receive a lunch allowance on workdays.

- Mental health support. To help you feel your best, we provide easy access to professional mental health services.

- Sports benefit. Enjoy an on-site gym or sports club stipend.

- Internal events. Join company-wide celebrations and team gatherings.

*Some benefits may vary depending on location.

title: Regional Operator Education Specialist
description:
Mission 

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose 

As Regional Operator Education Specialist you are responsible for the quality and delivery of onboarding for clinical operators across your region, ensuring training maintains a consistently high standard. You support and quality-assure the work carried out by Clinic Trainers, and act as the escalation point for clinical training matters, so that methods, delivery, and assessments stay aligned with global standards.

You also contribute to the maintenance of training programs and content, adapting them for local market needs based on central guidelines and frameworks. This is a competency-based training and safety function.

A note on this role 

Medical Education at Neko is growing and its structure is still developing. This is an interim appointment, and the scope described here may change as the wider function takes shape. We will be open with you about any changes as they happen.

What You'll Deliver 

Onboarding quality and escalation 

- Ensure clinical operator onboarding is delivered to a high and consistent standard across your region, aligned with central guidelines and member safety requirements.

- Run the onboarding cycle: confirm incoming starters with Recruitment, allocate trainers, and monitor daily trainee progress, stepping in early where progression is slow.

- Hold the decision to pass, extend, or offboard a trainee in your region, alongside the Lead Operator team.

- Act as the regional escalation point for clinical training quality and safety matters, triaging every case on first pass to distinguish a genuine safety risk from a standard performance gap, and seeing it through to closure including structured improvement plans.

Support and coach Clinic Trainers 

- Provide guidance, feedback, and support to Clinic Trainers on training methodology, delivery, and assessment.

- Hold trainers in your region to one national standard, working with Lead Operators so operational needs are met at the same time.

- Follow up on trainer performance and development.

- Support Clinic Trainers in completing Impact Reviews for existing clinical staff in line with Neko’s pillars.

Maintain and adapt training programs 

- Maintain training programs and materials as requested, including Sana content, and adapt them to local market needs while staying aligned with global standards and following approval guidelines.

- Work from one shared source with your counterpart region rather than maintaining separate regional versions, and flag content gaps and inconsistencies centrally rather than resolving them locally in isolation.

- Deliver or coordinate key clinical skills training within your region, for example Gen II retrofit training, and provide training-plan input into clinic launches and retrofits.

Monitor training quality and drive improvement 

- Observe training delivery, provide structured feedback, and follow up on what changes as a result.

- Run regional training audits and benchmarks against the national standard, identifying gaps and putting forward improvement proposals, including corrective action where an audit finding requires it.

- Oversee trainers’ records of staff competency sign-off. No operator works unsupervised on a new device until sign-off is confirmed.

- Feed hiring and training trends back to Recruitment so screening improves from what is seen downstream in training.

Partner across the business 

- Work closely with clinic leadership and relevant support functions so training meets operational needs as well as the clinical standard, and act as a regional training voice with Recruitment, clinic leads, and cluster management, syncing regularly to stay aligned nationally.

- Work closely with Clinical Development, participating in product launch handovers and acting as the educational link for your region, including developing training materials for new devices and SOPs when requested and supporting rollout to trainers and operators on the ground.

Minimum Qualifications 

- Healthcare professional with at least two years of clinical experience.

- Significant post-registration experience in a fast-paced, high-volume clinical setting.

- Demonstrated clinical leadership, formal or informal.

- Existing trainer or competency sign-off experience within a Neko clinic, or equivalent clinical procedure competency such as phlebotomy or ECG.

Preferred Qualifications 

- Experience managing clinical teams or trainers, including performance management across multiple sites.

- Track record in competency-based training and assessment.

- Experience developing or scaling training frameworks to support clinic expansion.

- Cross-functional collaboration with Recruitment, Operations, or Education teams.

- A postgraduate certification in a specialist clinical area or in leadership.

Key competencies 

- Strong communication and a coaching mindset

- Sound clinical judgement under ambiguity

- A collaborative approach with operators, clinic leads, and trainers

- Adaptability to new processes and policies

- Attention to detail in competency checks and training materials

- Organisational skills across multiple concurrent onboarding cycles

- A proactive, problem-solving approach to gaps in knowledge or process

Working conditions

title: Engagement Director - Strategic Accounts
description:

The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the center of that transformation. title: Head of Product
description:
About Us 

We are passionate industry experts in the property risk, compliance and safety management industry providing our leading end-to-end solution QUOODA – A platform for property owners and managers to maintain and manage a single source of truth for their complete property portfolio, covering commercial, residential, education, health, financial, tech, and telecoms sectors. 

Our platform is used by over 8000 users across trusted industry leaders and is responsible for managing several of the UK's most iconic buildings, such as London's O2 Arena, The Shard, One Blackfriars, and The Cheese Grater to name just a few. 

The goal of QUOODA is to make it quicker and easier to manage property risk and compliance, providing key information at your fingertips in real-time covering Health & Safety, Fire Safety, Environmental impact, Asset Management, Work Permits and more. 

The Team 

Our team is focused on delivering an industry leading platform for our users and providing them with the right features to simplify their tasks. To do this, the team is fully cross-functional and follows agile best practices in a highly collaborative environment - Taking ownership of the platform architecture, infrastructure, and application lifecycle following the 'Build It, Ship It, Own It' philosophy. 

We currently have several teams made up of engineers, testers, and product owners, and are expanding these as we move closer to our scalability and growth targets. This is an exciting time to join our team, as there are great opportunities to make your mark and influence how we do things as we progress with our expansion. 

The Role 

As Head of Product, you are the voice, validator and external face of QUOODA. Engineering owns what gets built and why; you bring the customer and commercial judgement they need to make those decisions well, and you are accountable for ensuring the product meets the bar before it reaches customers. Day to day, your closest working relationships are with the CTO and Director of Engineering: you keep them unblocked, informed and well-connected to the commercial and customer context they need. You are the product's spokesperson externally to customers, to sales and new business, and to customer success and you facilitate a direct, unfiltered relationship between engineering and the wider business. You do not sit in the middle: you remove friction, surface context, and validate outcomes. 

Key Responsibilities 

Product direction and voice 

- Set and communicate product strategy. Curate and communicate the QUOODA v2 roadmap, reflecting engineering decisions and ensuring the rationale is clearly articulated to the business and market. 

- Be the spokesperson for QUOODA. Represent the product internally and externally through demos, briefings, webinars, customer councils, sales conversations and analyst or prospect engagements. 

- Work closely with the CTO and Director of Engineering. Be their primary point of contact for commercial and customer context. Keep them informed of business priorities, market signals and customer feedback so they can make well-grounded decisions without being pulled into business-facing meetings themselves. Flag blockers, misalignments and communication gaps early. 

- Facilitate prioritisation. Facilitate prioritisation conversations between engineering, commercial and customers. Bring domain and customer context to those decisions, and ensure engineering has what it needs to make well-informed calls. 

Commercial, customer success and sales partnership 

- Enable sales and new business. Equip the commercial team with messaging, positioning, demo narratives and answers to the hard questions, so they can win against incumbents and triple our customer base by 2030. 

- Partner with customer success. Translate adoption signals, support themes and renewal risk into product decisions, and give CS the roadmap clarity they need to retain and grow accounts. 

The v1-to-v2 migration 

- Support engineering in leading the migration of 70 customers from QUOODA v1 to v2. Own the customer-facing communication and experience of the migration. Be the named, accountable point of contact for customers throughout the transition, ensuring engineering has the business and customer context needed to sequence and execute it well. 

- Surface migration risk to engineering. Ensure engineering has unfiltered customer insight to inform their parity decisions. Own the customer-facing communication of each change — what is different, why, and what support is available, once engineering has made those calls. 

- Lead the UAT process for QUOODA v2. Be the primary voice from the customer and business perspective on whether the product is ready. Sign off that it meets the bar commercially and functionally in partnership with engineering who hold the technical quality bar. The go/no-go decision is a shared call, and it is explicit. 

- Curate the backlog of known issues. Turn five years of accumulated, hard-won knowledge about v1's gaps into clear intent for v2. 

Working in an AI-native SDLC 

- Surface context, not tickets. Surface customer problems, commercial outcomes and real-world constraints in a form that is immediately useful to engineers and AI agents. The goal is to enrich engineering's intent, not to originate it. 

- Represent the product-engineering model externally. Help customers, partners and the wider business understand how our product-engineering model works and why it produces better outcomes. Engineering owns the operating model itself; your role is to make it legible and credible to the outside world. 

Requirements 

Essential 

- Demonstrable product leadership experience in B2B / enterprise SaaS, ideally with a complex, configurable platform. 

- A credible, confident external presence, comfortable being the face of a product with customers, prospects, sales and CS. 

- Strong commercial instinct: you understand how product decisions drive pipeline, win rates, retention and growth. 

- Experience owning a major product transition, migration or re-platforming with a live customer base. 

- Fluency with (or genuine enthusiasm to embrace) an AI-native, agentic software development lifecycle: working alongside AI coding agents, expressing intent rather than writing exhaustive specs, and evaluating AI-built software. 

Highly desirable 

- Regulated domain experience, ideally in GRC, risk, compliance, audit, or adjacent regulated enterprise software. 

- Familiarity with API-first, cloud-native product architectures. 

- Hands-on comfort with AI tooling: prototyping, prompting, and defining evaluations to assess output quality. 

- Experience in a private-equity backed or high-growth scale-up environment. 

Benefits 

- Competitive salary (depending on experience). 

- 25 days annual leave (excluding UK bank holidays). 

- 5% Matched company pension. 

- Vitality private health insurance (includes Vitality membership). 

- 4x salary life cover. 

- Perk Pal retail discounts. 

- Regular virtual and in-person social events. 

If you are a strategic thinker with a passion for writing high-scale, secure, cloud native software, this is an exciting opportunity to grow and help shape the future of our product, platform, and culture. 

Sustainware is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Product Owner – Trust Services (eIDAS2, EUDI Wallet & Trust Platform) (f/m/d)
description:
IDnow is a leader in digital identity and fraud prevention in Europe with a mission to transform trust into the most powerful asset in the digital world, empowering enterprises with AI-driven, SaaS-based identity solutions that deliver scalable security, adaptive compliance, and real-time fraud prevention . Through its broad portfolio of digital identity and fraud prevention solutions, IDnow establishes, maintains and enriches trust throughout the customer journey, ensuring businesses can confidently and securely operate while leveraging digital identity to drive growth, security and scalability. 

The company has offices in Germany, United Kingdom, Romania and France , and is backed by renowned institutional investors, including Corsair Capital and Seventure Partners. Its portfolio of international clients spans a wide range of end markets including financial services, telecommunications, travel & mobility, gaming, and other industries. 

This position is based in Berlin/Munich, Germany or Rennes, France. 

IDnow is looking for Product Owner – Trust Services (f/m/d) to own the product direction, backlog and outcomes for a technical product area within IDnow’s Digital Identity and Trust Services portfolio. Working with a dedicated Scrum Team, this role turns customer, operational, regulatory and engineering input into a clear product goal, an ordered backlog and valuable, usable increments that can be released and operated safely. 

The most critical aspect of this role is serving as the accountable product interface between the Trust Services domain and Engineering: understanding the system boundaries, APIs, integrations, data flows and non-functional requirements well enough to make sound trade-offs, remove ambiguity and ensure that security, privacy, resilience, auditability and regulatory obligations are built into the product from the beginning. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Own the product goal, roadmap and backlog : prioritize by value, risk, dependencies and learning; keep decisions transparent. 

- Drive Scrum outcomes : lead refinement, support Planning and Reviews, clarify Sprint Goals, and use delivery metrics to improve flow. 

- Turn needs into buildable requirements : define user/system journeys, domain concepts, business rules, APIs, data states, errors, acceptance criteria and testable non-functional requirements – without over-prescribing implementation. 

- Partner on solution quality : work with Engineering, Architecture, Security, QA and Operations on service boundaries, technical debt, scalability, performance, availability, resilience, observability, incidents and operational readiness. 

- Own data, integration and lifecycle design : govern identity and audit-data flows, access, protection and retention; shape secure, interoperable APIs, including authentication, encryption, versioning, error handling and documentation. 

- Support releases and continuous improvement : define readiness, migrations, cutovers, deprecation, feature flags and rollback; participate in incident reviews and prioritize recurring quality, security and operational issues. 

- Translate regulation into product decisions : apply eIDAS2, EUDI Wallet, QES, QEAA/EAA, identity-proofing and trust-service requirements with Compliance, Legal, Risk and Trust Services SMEs, tracking adoption, reliability, quality, delivery flow and compliance readiness. 

- Collaborate across functions: align with Scrum Team s , Engineering leadership, Architecture, Security, SRE/Operations, Trust Services, Product, Compliance/Legal/Risk/Data Protection, Commercial and Customer Success, as well as relevant partners, relying parties and standards bodies. 

Preferred Experience 

- 4+ years of experience in Product Ownership, Technical Product Management, Business Analysis or similar roles in software and service delivery, including direct responsibility for backlog quality and product outcomes. 

- Hands-on experience working in Scrum or a comparable agile delivery model: ability to define a Product Goal, order a Product Backlog, write clear product backlog items, set acceptance criteria, participate in refinement and reviews, and make timely scope and priority decisions. 

- Strong technical fluency in modern software products and integrations, including REST APIs, JSON/Open API, authentication and authorization, OAuth2/OIDC concepts, webhooks or event streams, data models, service boundaries, API lifecycle and backward-compatible change. 

- Demonstrable experience working with regulated software and services, translating regulatory, security, privacy and audit requirements into actionable product requirements and delivery decisions, while balancing compliance, customer value, usability, scalability and time to market. 

- Practical understanding of secure software and service delivery: threat and risk thinking, software security, access control, encryption, secrets and key management, vulnerability handling, logging/monitoring, incident response, resilience and software supply-chain considerations. 

- Practical understanding of data lifecycle and privacy-by-design for identity and trust services, including data minimization, purpose limitation, sensitive evidence, retention and deletion, evidence, archival, data residency, audit trails and access transparency. 

- Ability to work with Engineering on system-level trade-offs without needing to be the implementing engineer, and to distinguish product decisions, architecture decisions, implementation choices, technical debt and operational risk. 

- Experience with service operations and lifecycle management, including release readiness, SLO or service-quality thinking, incident triage, post-incident learning, customer-impact assessment, migration, deprecation and support enablement. 

- Experience in regulated industries (e.g., financial services, telecom, public sector, payments, KYC/AML, digital identity, electronic signatures, PKI or trust services) is a strong plus, as is familiarity with eIDAS2, EUDI Wallets, ETSI standards or QTSP operating models. 

Perks & Benefits 

- Health & Wellbeing: Use your full access to the mental health platform nilo, including 1on1 sessions. 

- We value personal and professional development: make full use of Udemy, our training platform with 24/7 access and unlimited licences. 

- We make your remote work comfy: we provide support on equipment and offer flexible working hours. 

- We value collaboration & love to come together: regular onsite gatherings, internal initiatives and summer parties to connect across teams. 

- May your family require your attention or other reasons apply: use the benefits of our parental leave policy or our sabbatical programme. 

- In addition to the perks & benefits above, we offer specific benefits that differ between our locations.

- Indemnité téléphonique de 30 € 

- Indemnité Internet de 36 € 

- Mutuelle d’entreprise

title: Technical Writer
description:
About Alta Ares

Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission 

As Technical Writer, you will own the documentation of Alta Ares' product suite — producing the manuals, user guides, interface specifications, and operational references that enable military operators, system integrators, and institutional clients to deploy and use Alta Ares' platforms with confidence.

In defence, documentation is not a nice-to-have. A military operator in a contested environment cannot call the helpdesk. A procurement officer reviewing an acceptance package expects documentation that is precise, complete, and unambiguous. Your work is the last line of clarity between a complex, cutting-edge system and the person who has to operate it under pressure.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, and the Pre & Post Sales team — translating deeply technical content into structured, accessible, operationally relevant documentation. This is a high-craft, high-ownership role in a company where the quality of your writing directly affects operational outcomes.

Product Documentation — User Guides & Operator Manuals 

- Own the full suite of end-user documentation for Alta Ares' product portfolio: operator manuals, quick-start guides, field reference cards, and system overviews

- Write clear, structured, and operationally grounded documentation for military end-users — adapting tone, level of detail, and format to the audience (drone operator, system administrator, field commander)

- Develop and maintain documentation for each product line: ISR module, C-UAS platform, MLOps stack, GCS interface, and ground equipment

- Produce multilingual documentation in English and French — ensuring accuracy and consistency across both versions

- Maintain a versioned documentation library aligned with each product release and firmware update

Interface & System Specifications 

- Document software interfaces, system architectures, and hardware integration specifications in collaboration with Engineering

- Produce interface control documents (ICDs), system description documents (SDDs), and integration guides for system integrators and institutional clients

- Translate engineering schematics, API references, and architecture diagrams into human-readable specifications accessible to non-specialist audiences

- Maintain up-to-date configuration guides, parameter references, and software release notes for each product version

- Support the Engineering team in documenting internal technical standards and development guidelines

Operational & Field Documentation 

- Develop field-ready documentation adapted to operational environments: laminated quick-reference cards, checklists, and compact field guides

- Produce pre-flight checklists, maintenance procedures, and troubleshooting guides for UAV platforms and C-UAS systems

- Create training materials and operational scenario guides for use during client onboarding, field demonstrations, and exercises

- Ensure all field documentation meets the usability requirements of military audiences: clear hierarchy, unambiguous language, and actionable step-by-step instructions

Documentation Lifecycle & Quality Management 

- Own the documentation lifecycle end-to-end: planning, drafting, review, validation, versioning, and publication

- Establish and enforce documentation standards across Alta Ares: style guide, terminology glossary, formatting conventions, and review processes

- Coordinate review cycles with Engineering, Product, and Pre & Post Sales teams — ensuring technical accuracy before publication

- Manage the documentation repository in Notion and ensure all documents are findable, versioned, and access-controlled appropriately

- Track and incorporate feedback from field deployments, client reviews, and post-sales observations into documentation updates

Client-Facing Delivery Documentation 

- Produce documentation packages for client deliverables: acceptance test procedures, delivery dossiers, and contractual documentation requirements

- Support the preparation of responses to RFP documentation requirements and compliance matrices

- Contribute to the development of training packages for institutional clients and partner integrators

- Ensure client-facing documentation meets applicable defence documentation standards and contractual specifications

Candidate Profile - Experience 

- 3–5 years of experience in technical writing — with a strong focus on product documentation, user manuals, or operational guides

- Prior experience documenting hardware-software integrated systems — mandatory : you must be comfortable with complex, multi-component products

- Background in defence, aerospace, robotics, deeptech, or dual-use is a strong plus — you understand the operational context in which your documentation will be used

- Experience producing documentation for non-specialist end-users (operators, field technicians) as well as technical audiences (engineers, integrators)

- Prior exposure to documentation lifecycle management and versioning in a product environment

title: Senior Jet Engine Design Engineer – Interceptor Drones
description:
About Alta Ares

Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

About the Role 
We are building next-generation interceptor drones and are looking for a Senior Jet Engine Design Engineer to lead the development of small-scale jet propulsion systems (12–25 kg thrust class), from concept to flight-ready hardware. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a fast-moving startup environment where speed and iteration matter more than lengthy upfront studies.

Responsibilities: 

- Design and develop new small jet engines (12–25 kg thrust range) in-house, optimized for very low production cost

- Own the aerodynamic design of turbine components, balancing performance, manufacturability, and cost

- Design a large portion of the turbine for metal 3D printing (additive manufacturing), leveraging design-for-AM principles to reduce part count, weight, and cost

- Work closely with 3D printing operations to define printable geometries, tolerances, post-processing, and qualify parts for flight use

- Drive a rapid, fail-fast iteration process: build, test, learn, and redesign quickly rather than relying on long analytical phases before prototyping

- Integrate propulsion systems into airframes such as flying wings and other interceptor drone configurations, working with aerostructures and systems teams

- Apply and enforce design rules for operation in extreme environments (cold and hot climates, rain, humidity, icing conditions) to ensure engine reliability across the full operational envelope

- Contribute to engine testing (bench and flight), performance validation, and continuous design improvement

Candidate Profile: 

- Minimum 8 years of experience in jet engine / gas turbine design, with a proven track record of having designed and delivered engine models (not just component-level work)

- Strong hands-on experience with small jet engines in the 12–25 kg thrust class

- Solid global understanding of jet engine architecture: compressor, combustor, turbine, fuel system, controls, and their interactions

- Experience designing turbine/engine components for metal additive manufacturing (DfAM), and practical knowledge of metal 3D printing processes and constraints

- Comfortable working in a rapid-iteration, fail-fast development culture rather than a traditional long-cycle aerospace process

- Experience integrating propulsion systems into airframes (flying wing or similar unconventional platforms is a strong plus)

- Knowledge of design requirements for extreme operating environments (temperature extremes, precipitation, icing)

- Ability to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced startup team, wearing multiple hats when needed

Nice to Have 

- Experience with UAV/drone propulsion specifically (vs. manned aviation)

- Familiarity with low-cost manufacturing strategies for defense/dual-use hardware

- Prior startup or skunkworks experience

title: Account Manager – Retention Specialist
description:
Notre mission ⚖️ 

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

About the job

Mistral is hiring a Head of FDE Learning Programs to build the learning system for one of the company’s fastest-growing organizations. Mistral is scaling its FDE organization from its first hire to several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers within two years. Your mandate is to make capability grow as fast as headcount without lowering the bar for customer work.

You will own: 

- Learning content: Build practical learning across three areas: technical skills, strategic and business capabilities, and product enablement.

- Onboarding: Build a clear path from a new hire’s first week to independent customer work.

- Technical bootcamps: Turn new products, research, and field methods into practical training for customer work.

- What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

- Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

- Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

- We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

- No politics. Low ego, high standards.

- We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

About you

You have helped build a learning, enablement, or capability function for a technical organization during rapid growth. You can start as the first dedicated owner, deliver useful programs immediately, and build the team and operating model needed to serve several hundred people.

- 

- You are technically fluent enough to work credibly with AI engineers, Product, and Science, inspect the substance of a program, and challenge material that is unclear or outdated.

- You have designed programs that work across cohorts, regions, and experience levels without reducing the content to generic training.

- 

- You can lead work across senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, managers, and operational partners without relying on reporting lines.

- You can make firm trade-offs when hiring demand, expert capacity, and program quality compete for attention.

- You pay attention to the full learner experience, including communications, scheduling, practice, feedback, and manager follow-through.

- You use evidence to decide which programs to expand, revise, or stop.

- You communicate clearly with executives, managers, technical experts, and learners.

- You are fluent in English and can work with teams across regions and time zones.

Ideally, you have

- Scaled a one-person or small learning function into a team and program that served hundreds of technical employees.

- Built onboarding that kept pace with rapid hiring in an engineering, FDE, solutions, consulting, or professional-services organization.

- Designed and operated technical bootcamps or other cohort-based learning programs.

- Worked in technical DevRel, developer education, or a related role built around demos, code examples, workshops, and practitioner communities.

- Built role- and level-based curricula connected to skills frameworks or career progression.

- Managed a global program with contributors and learners across multiple regions.

- Worked closely with Product, Engineering, Science, People, and customer-facing teams.

- Designed practical assessments, readiness standards, or certification where appropriate.

- Used learning platforms, knowledge systems, AI coaches, or program-operations tooling.

- Worked in AI/ML or another technically complex and fast-changing field.

Why this role matters

Mistral is compressing years of organization growth into two. An FDE organization of several hundred people cannot depend on manager-by-manager onboarding, one-off sessions, and informal access to experts. If learning capacity trails hiring, ramp times would lengthen, standards would diverge, and teams would repeat the same mistakes across regions.

This role will build the programs, teaching network, and systems at the same pace as the organization. Two years from now, success would mean several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers working from shared standards, learning new capabilities quickly, and improving the system with evidence from customer work.
